bodytext:
Every fifteen minutes, forty-six stations along the Anbach send the institute one reading each: water level, temperature, dissolved oxygen, turbidity. On its own a single value says almost nothing. Held against the twelve years behind it, the same value tells us whether the gravel beds below the weir are silting up again.

What a station measures

The standard mast carries four sensors and a logger. Level and temperature run continuously. Oxygen and turbidity are recorded on the same interval but calibrated by hand twice a year, because a drifting oxygen probe is worse than no probe at all.

  • Water level, to the centimetre
  • Temperature at two depths
  • Dissolved oxygen
  • Turbidity, as a stand-in for suspended load

Why the raw series is published too

Marnau publishes the unsmoothed series next to the cleaned one. Anyone checking a flood peak against our own report can see exactly which values we discarded, and why. The data licence asks only that the series is credited.
